intent: Restore the iteration 9 geometry exactly (outer sensors at x = ±0.03, y = 0.04, 15 mm spacing, 0.016 footprint, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, 0.18 m x 0.12 m body, 0.8 kg). This is the best verified platform (271.06, 8 of 20 oval completions) and is the safest choice for the unseen final track. Expected: a score at or near 271 on the development tracks, with oval completions held near 8 of 20.
learning: Iteration 10 showed wheel_track 0.14 cut oval completions from 8 to 3 and dropped the score to 215, so a wider track reduces the steering gain too far for this controller. Slalom line loss of about 1 persists across every geometry and controller variant tried, so the remaining gap is likely controller-side rather than geometry-side. For future work, a narrower track (0.10 to 0.11 m) is the untested direction that would raise steering gain, and it should be tested as a single change.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design raced here is the one scored on the unseen track. I am choosing the most robust verified geometry rather than testing a new lever. Iteration 9 (wheel_track 0.12, outer sensors at x = ±0.03, y = 0.04, 15 mm spacing, 0.016 footprint, 0.18 m / 0.8 kg body) is the best raced result at 271.06. Iteration 8 reproduced iteration 7 exactly, so results are deterministic for a fixed design. Iteration 10 tested wheel_track 0.14 on the same platform and scored 215.32, a drop of 56 points. Oval completions fell from 8 of 20 to 3 of 20, and oval progress fell from 0.91 to 0.80. The lower steering gain from the wider track hurt the completion term that dominates the score. The Integrator's conditional rule for this case says to return wheel_track to 0.12, and the data supports that. The R1 feedback's 'keep 0.14' request is contradicted by iteration 10's outcome, so I do not follow it. Slalom line loss stays at about 1 on every design, but I will not gamble the final race on an untested fix. Body length, body width, mass, footprint, row position and spread all stay at their verified iteration 9 values, since body changes cost progress in iterations 2 and 3. I expect a score near 271 on the development tracks. The unseen track is the real uncertainty, and the main protection is keeping the design that has produced the most completions.
